name: Pink Street (Rua Nova do Carvalho)
seoTitle: Pink Street, Cais do Sodré: Worth It on a Port Day?
tagline: A short pink-painted street behind Cais do Sodré station: quiet by day, packed with bar crowds at night.

description.short: Rua Nova do Carvalho, known as Pink Street, is a short street of bars one block behind Cais do Sodré station, painted pink in 2011. By day it is quiet and takes five minutes to see; it fills up late at night, especially from Thursday to Saturday.
description.full:
Pink Street is a night-time street. If your ship sails before evening, set your expectations accordingly: by day Rua Nova do Carvalho is a short stretch of pink-painted road with shuttered bars and a few people taking photos. It takes about five minutes to see and is not worth a special trip on its own.

It does make sense as a quick detour when you are already at Cais do Sodré. From the terminal, walk about 26 minutes west along the flat riverside, past Praça do Comércio; the street runs one block behind Cais do Sodré station, under the stone arch that carries Rua do Alecrim overhead. A taxi takes about 10 minutes. Combine it with lunch at the Time Out Market or a look round the traditional Mercado da Ribeira, both a couple of minutes away, or with the train to Belém from the station.

For a photo of the pink surface without people, go in the morning. From late afternoon, bar tables and drinkers start to cover it.

The street comes alive only after dark. Bars open from late afternoon or evening, the crowd builds from about 22:00 and it peaks on Thursday to Saturday nights, when the street is packed and loud. That makes it relevant mainly to passengers on overnight calls or late departures. If you go, keep your all-aboard time in mind, carry phones and wallets in front pockets, and plan the way back: about 26 minutes' walk east along the river, or a taxi or ride-hailing car, which can be slow to find at closing time on weekend nights.

Skip it if you dislike crowds. Daytime visitors looking for atmosphere will find more along the Ribeira das Naus promenade or uphill in Chiado.

Context: this was the centre of the port's sailors' nightlife for much of the 20th century, and the pink paint arrived in 2011 as part of a local effort to revive the area.
description.history: Cais do Sodré was reclaimed and extended along the river from the mid-19th century. From the 1920s its closeness to the port made Rua Nova do Carvalho the centre of a nightlife aimed at sailors and dock workers, with bars and cabarets. Between the 1930s and the 1980s clubs such as Jamaica and the Texas Bar (now Music Box) opened here. In 2011 the Associação do Cais do Sodré, with the backing of Lisbon City Council, painted the road pink to mark a fresh start. In 2013 a project by architect José Adrião levelled the road with the pavements to make room for outdoor tables. Pensão Amor, once a rooming house used by sailors, is now a bar.
description.significance: The street is the clearest example of how Cais do Sodré turned from a port-side red-light district into one of Lisbon's main bar areas within a few years. Some old sailors' bars still trade next to newer cocktail bars, so both phases sit side by side. For a visitor it is a nightlife address and a quick photo stop, not a sight with anything to visit inside.

directions.general: Located in Cais do Sodré district, just off the waterfront between Time Out Market and Bairro Alto
directions.fromCruisePort: About 1.9 km and 26 minutes on foot, flat along the river to Cais do Sodré; Rua Nova do Carvalho is one block behind the station. Taxi about 8-10 minutes.
directions.publicTransport: Metro: Cais do Sodré (Green line - 2 min walk). Train: Cais do Sodré station. Tram: 15E, 18E, 25E. The street is pedestrian-only.
directions.parking: No parking on street itself. Public parking at Praça Dom Luís I (500m) or nearby garages.

openingTimes.currentStatus: Public street, open at all times

seasonal.notes: Bars generally open from late afternoon or evening and close in the early hours; hours vary by venue. Busiest Thursday to Saturday from about 22:00.

admissionPrices.notes: Free: it is a public street. You pay only for what you drink in the bars, and prices vary by venue.

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: 5–10 minutes by day; an evening if you are staying late
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Morning for an empty-street photo. After 22:00, Thursday to Saturday, for the nightlife.
busyPeriods: Thursday to Saturday nights, from about 22:00
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: By day the street is quiet and quick to see, so combine it with the Time Out Market, the Mercado da Ribeira or the train at Cais do Sodré. At night it gets very crowded: keep valuables in front pockets and plan your return to the ship before you go out.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 1 hour for a daytime look on foot (26 minutes each way); an evening for the nightlife
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Flat 26-minute riverside walk from the terminal, or about 10 minutes by taxi. The road was levelled with the pavements in 2013; many bars have a step at the door.
combinableWith: Train to Belém from Cais do Sodré
tips: By day the street takes five minutes to see; make the detour only if you are already at Cais do Sodré for the Time Out Market, the Mercado da Ribeira or a train.
Walk from the ship along the flat riverside via Praça do Comércio, about 26 minutes; the street is one block behind Cais do Sodré station.
For a photo of the pink road without crowds, go in the morning; in the evening the surface disappears under bar tables and people.
The nightlife starts late, building from about 22:00 and peaking Thursday to Saturday, so it suits overnight calls and late departures rather than a 17:00 sailing.
Keep phones and wallets in front pockets: the late-night crowds are dense.
Plan your return before you go out: the terminal is about 26 minutes' walk east along the river, and taxis can be slow to find at closing time on weekend nights.
If the street disappoints in daylight, walk a few minutes east to the Ribeira das Naus promenade or uphill along Rua do Alecrim to Chiado.

highlights: Pink-painted road between Travessa do Corpo Santo and Praça de São Paulo
Stone arch carrying Rua do Alecrim over the street
Former sailors' bars, such as Pensão Amor, next to newer cocktail bars
Busiest Thursday to Saturday nights from about 22:00
One block from Cais do Sodré station, the Time Out Market and the Mercado da Ribeira
facilities: Cais do Sodré station (metro, trains, ferries) one block away
No public toilets on the street

accessibility.mobilityNotes: The road is level with the pavements. Individual bars may have steps or narrow doorways, and the street is very crowded on weekend nights.
